title: sc-security-audit manifest
description: How one repository is security-audited. The posture decides everything downstream, so it is the one required key: third-party posture forbids building, installing or resolving the code under audit, and guessing that wrong is the mistake that executes it.

posture.description: in-house: findings are defects with a remediation path. third-party: findings are an adopt / pin / vendor / reject decision, and the audit is read-only by construction. Required when this file exists; inferred from the origin remote when it does not, falling to third-party.

asvs_level.description: OWASP ASVS level the secure-practice lane is judged at. Defaults to 1.

scope.description: include/exclude globs. An excluded path is unaudited, not passing, so exclusions belong here where they are reviewable.

exposure.description: Third-party posture: the surface this code will actually be given. Exploitability is scoped to it, because a vulnerable path that is never mounted is not a finding.

tools.description: Per-lane tool overrides. Absent means the lane defaults. A named tool that is not installed FAILs the lane, it never skips it.

baseline.description: Path to the suppression file. Every entry carries a justification and an expiry date; an expired suppression is itself a finding.

report_surface.description: The sc-nda-check surface the report is written for. The report quotes code, paths and secret names, so it is sensitive output in its own right.

severity_overrides.description: Per-rule or per-CWE severity adjustments, with a reason. Blanket downgrades are how a report stops being read.
